note: A world_buildings fragment (src/buildings.cpp): res/systems/ksp_system.json names it under "world_buildings_files" and the loader merges these entries into its own "world_buildings". Hand-authored -- utils/gen_systems.py emits only the reference, never this table, so regenerating the system JSON cannot clobber a coordinate; tests/test_buildings.cpp pins what reaches the game. lat_deg/lon_deg are DEGREES, lon east-positive, in the BODY's own equirect frame (equirect.h), so the same numbers on two bodies are the same place on each of them. Each BODY's default site is the first VAB_LAUNCH_PAD for that body (find_launch_site filters by body), and merged fragments come before a system's inline world_buildings -- so this table picks Kerbin's, Moho's and Duna's defaults. polar_pad sits AFTER the two surface pads, so it cannot win that race; no shipped system authors pads inline, so the merge-order rule itself stays pinned by the synthetic inline row in tests/test_buildings.cpp. moho_pad and duna_pad sit at Kerbin's coordinates: placeholders so off-world launches are reachable, not placed against any survey. ksc_runway IS placed against a survey (tmp/runway_probe.cpp, reports/runway-wheels2026_11_14): a 900x30 m footprint with 0.56 m of relief, 2.7 km from the pad. It carries VAB_LAUNCH_PAD so the picker/map/recovery see it, plus RUNWAY which selects the horizontal spawn pose; it sits AFTER main_space_port so the default site is unchanged. heading_deg spins the mesh's long axis (local +X); at this site faceAlong's axis pick lands X=east, so heading 5 deg matches the survey's east-based azimuth -- at another site that correspondence can flip (the spawn reads the actual building basis, so ship and mesh always agree). polar_pad came back with #1133 after #1063 deleted its row (the pad-polar scenario bed that used to park a hull there had already gone in e70d467c). It stands at 88.8 / 171.4, NOT lat 90: #1007 probed Kerbin's polar region and found the ground at the pole 328 m UNDER Kerbin's own sea, and this spot 12.6 km off the pole -- 1.2 deg on Kerbin's 600 km radius -- is the nearest dry flat ground, with 50.1 m of deck pinned in tests/test_buildings.cpp. (#1007 wrote that move up as 240 km and Eerbon's as 708 km; neither reproduces -- 1.2 deg and 3.1 deg of a 600 km world are 12.6 km and 32.5 km, so read the degrees, which are what the survey chose.) The offset is also the pad's job: a hull parked here reads 3.66 m/s of ground speed in [orbinfo] vel= against 175.0 m/s at main_space_port, so it starts almost at rest in the inertial frame instead of inheriting 175 m/s of eastward motion. It does not carry the old POLAR_PAD flag: find_launch_site read it until e70d467c removed that preferPolar path, nothing in src/ reads it now, and a pad 12.6 km from a pole is not a region label either.
